headline: Pretrained protein models are applied to site and variant prediction and then tested for failure modes
label: Protein Model Site And Variant
summary: New preprints pair protein language model applications with stress tests: relabeling invariance, embedding anisotropy and NMR shift errors expose limits of learned representations.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of pretrained protein and molecular models to prioritize sites, interfaces, ligands and mutations, with structural, thermodynamic or dynamic information added. Examples include AllositeUltra for apo and substrate-bound allosteric sites, HandShake for partner-specific interfaces via ProstT5, HieraPTM for functional phosphosites, DiffTernary for molecular glue docking, PULSE for context-aware steering, and an antisymmetric EvoPhi-DDG combined with JanusDDG for thermodynamically consistent stability prediction. What is new is the emphasis on diagnosing limits. Contact maps from protein language models collapse under amino-acid relabeling, severe embedding anisotropy degrades retrieval until ZCA is applied, and NMR 15N shifts show the largest errors at core residues with fast dynamics. Bonbon also reports zero-shot emergent binding-site and covalent-bond capabilities.
